newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Brief Ivorian oil dispute ends - state television.
newsitem.headline: Brief Ivorian oil dispute ends - state television.

text.p: A dispute between communities in and around the Ivory Coast's seaside town of Jacqueville and U.S. oil company United Meridian that disrupted off-shore drilling for 48 hours is over, state television reported.

The television said on Sunday that talks between UMIC, a subsidiary of Houston-based United Meridian Corp, and the local mayor had resolved the dispute over benefits for the local population from oil production on its doorstep.

"We are here for 25 years and we will work together during this 25 years and I hope that the population will be content with our aid in the long term," UMIC managing director Steve Thornton told the television.
"Give us a little time because we cannot do eveything at once," he said. "In the long term we will try to improve life here in these communes."

The mayor and a local dignitary questioned by the television listed supplies of drinking water in the coastal strip, repair of ferries crossing a nearby lagoon, upkeep of village access tracks and school and health facilities among local demands.
Employment of locals was another issue, the television said.
Thornton, whose company is part of a consortium operating in the area, held talks with the mayor and other locals in Jacqueville.
The television said that the 48-hour stoppage had cost production worth 100 million CFA francs (about $170,000).
